headline: Given each ecosystem's documented answer to a high-cardinality value the field converges, `cn` returns to parity with `cnfast`, and only `@yak/solid` stays behind — its reactive wrapper is not something best practice can hand-write away.

microbench.why: `vanilla-solid` leads at 2.19M renders/s. Given best practice the recoveries are large: `cn` reaches 1.60M from 243,000 and `tailwind-merge` 1.55M from 477,000, both by hand-splitting the value out of the class, and `cn` returns to within 3% of `cnfast`'s 1.64M. `next-yak` at 792,000 and `yak-solid` at 113,000 are unchanged from the naive case, since the CSS-variable path is what they already compiled to. That parity is the point on React and the problem on Solid: 9.58 of yak-solid's 11.3 ms is framework work for a per-element memo.

autocannon.why: `next-yak-css` at 1,280 req/s leads with `vanilla` at 1,200; `cnfast` at 1,160, `vanilla-solid` at 1,170 and `cn` at 1,090 arrive there by hand-written discipline. `yak-solid` at 94 req/s is unchanged from the naive case.

attribution.why: `vanilla-solid` at 0.714 ms and `next-yak-css` at 0.736 ms are the floor. `cn` falls to 0.312 ms of lib self-time from 4.20 ms in the naive case, and `goober` to 0.489 ms from 6.18 ms — the two clearest single measurements of what the hand-written workaround buys. `yak-solid` at 11.3 ms is again 85% framework.

hydrate.why: `vanilla-solid` at 31.4 ms leads, the React lanes cluster near 48 ms, and `yak-solid` at 95.4 ms rebuilds its per-element memos. `goober` at 86.1 ms is back with the field, having stopped inserting a rule per value.

inp.why: The React field is flat between 6.9 ms and 9.5 ms, and `cn` at 7.3 ms is back beside `cnfast` — the 17.0 ms it paid on the naive case is gone with the arbitrary value. `vanilla-solid` at 7.1 ms is unremarkable here.

mount.why: `vanilla-solid` mounts in 22.1 ms and the React lanes cluster between 63 ms and 96 ms — with the value on an inline style there is no sheet to inject, so `goober` lands at 82.4 ms instead of 1,290 ms.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane. Every lane in this case ends with a static class plus an inline value, which is the shape the style engine handles in one match.

payload.why: `vanilla` at 5,502 gz B is the floor and the CSS column collapses for everyone: `goober` ships 189 B against 9,145 B in the naive case, and the utility lanes drop about 5 kB each once the arbitrary-value utilities stop being generated. `cn` at 18,436 B remains the heaviest, 13,054 B of it library JS.

nsweep.why: `vanilla-solid` holds 1.77 ms at 4,000 instances, `cnfast` 2.66 ms and `tailwind-merge` 2.68 ms — best practice flattens every line that bent in the naive case, `cn` included at 2.80 ms. `yak-solid` at 39.1 ms is the exception, since its slope comes from the wrapper rather than from the value.

crossCase: The best-practice corner of the trio with the Examples `dyn-translate` and `dyn-inline`. The lanes that recover here do it by hand: the developer splits the static class from the dynamic inline style, replicating per component what a compiler could do once. `goober` moves 169,000 to 877,000 renders/s, `tailwind-merge` 477,000 to 1.55M, and `cn` 243,000 to 1.60M — the largest recovery in the case, because its whole loss was the arbitrary-value cache miss. `next-yak` reads 792,000 either way because its CSS-variable path is already the same code, and `yak-solid` reads 113,000 either way for the same reason.
